To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 5 different disease-causing germ-line mutations in 7 Finnish families with Li–Fraumeni syndrome: 4 in the TP53 gene (5 families) and 1 in CHK2 (2 families).
we have identified 2 new families with Li-Faumeni syndrome, one of which has a mutation in CHK2 gene, and that we have identified two new families with Li- Fraumeni-like syndrome.
the frequency of p53 mutations in LFS is similar to that reported in the literature and the frequency of CHK2 mutations in LFS was higher than expected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of mutations in the p, 53, CHK2 and CHK1 genes.
the genetic analysis of Finnish Li-Fraumenis syndrome (LFS) patients, and the role of CHK2 in cancer predisposition.
the genetic analysis of the Li-Fraumenis syndrome, a rare cancer predisposition syndrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the p53 gene is the major gene in LFS, but CHK2 is also an important gene in a subset of LFS patients, and the role of CHK1 remains to be clarified.
p53 is the main cause of LFS in Finland, and CHK2 is the second cause.
p53 is a gene for LFS and Li-Fraumenie-like syndrome, and that CHK2 is a gene for Li-Fraumenis-like syndrome, and possibly also for LFS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in 15% of the Finnish LFS families, mutations in the p 53 gene were found, and in 5% of the LFS families, a mutation in the CHK2 was identified.
the p53 gene accounts for 11.4% of the Finnish families and that the CHK2 gene is involved in at least 4.5% of the families.
p53 mutations are still the most common cause of LFS, but CHK2 mutations may account for a substantial fraction of families with LFS-like phenotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CHK2 gene may contribute to the genetic predisposition to LFS in a small proportion of families.
in families with Li-Faumeni syndrome and Li-Faumen-like syndrome, the most common cause is p53 mutation.
in the future, when a new family is suspected of having a germ-line p53 mutation, a mutation in the CHK2 or CHK1 gene should also be sought.
